comments.body:
## Phase 1 exit — RCA: the downgrade is REPRODUCED on `/review/`, not merely unguarded

The ticket recorded "no plaintext Location has been OBSERVED from these three surfaces; this is a
missing structural guarantee, not a reproduced downgrade." **That is now superseded by direct
evidence.** An unauthenticated probe of the deployed edge reproduces the downgrade on `/review/`.

### Live evidence (unauthenticated, no credential transmitted)

    $ curl -sS -o /dev/null -D - https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/review/health/
    HTTP/2 307
    location: http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/health

    $ curl … /review/webhook/   -> HTTP/2 307  location: http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/webhook
    $ curl … /review/rerun/     -> HTTP/2 307  location: http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/rerun

Same shape as 79b2: a **307** (method AND body preserved) carrying an **absolute `http://`
same-host** Location. Clients differ on whether they keep `Authorization` across a same-host
scheme change, so a client that keeps it retransmits its credential in plaintext — the review-bot
authenticates callers with an `X-Rebar-Token` header (`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:63`), which is
exactly such a credential.

    $ curl … /opcert/jobs/      -> HTTP/2 403   (no Location)
    $ curl … /opcert/health/    -> HTTP/2 403   (no Location)

`/opcert/`'s fail-closed `X-Opcert-Guard` check (`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:118-123`) rejects
an unauthenticated probe **before** proxying, so the live probe cannot reach the app. That is a
reachability answer, not an exemption — see the local reproduction below.

### Confirmed mechanism — this is 79b2's root cause B, on two more services

Answering the ticket's explicit open question ("`/review/` and `/opcert/` should be checked for the
same posture rather than presumed affected or unaffected"): **both share the broken posture.
Neither is exempt.**

`FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` is set for exactly one service — `mcp` (`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:357`,
mirrored in the blue-green path at `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:380`). It is **unset** for
`review-bot` (`docker-compose.yml:75`) and for `opcert` (`docker-compose.yml:266`). uvicorn reads it
natively, defaults it to `"127.0.0.1"`, and wraps the app in
`ProxyHeadersMiddleware(trusted_hosts=<that>)`. Both services run **inside containers** published on
host loopback — `127.0.0.1:${REVIEW_BOT_PORT:-8000}:8000` (`:97`) and `127.0.0.1:8090:8080` (`:298`)
— so host nginx's connection arrives from the **docker bridge gateway**, not `127.0.0.1`. The peer
is untrusted, `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` is dropped, `scope["scheme"]` stays `"http"`, and
Starlette's `redirect_slashes` builds its redirect as `URL(scope=…)` — an **absolute** URL whose
scheme comes from that scope.

Discriminating experiment (local, both real apps, one variable changed — the trust list):

    review-bot /health/       trusted='127.0.0.1'  -> 307 http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/health
    review-bot /health/       trusted='*'          -> 307 https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/health
    opcert     /opcert/jobs/  trusted='127.0.0.1'  -> 307 http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/opcert/jobs
    opcert     /opcert/jobs/  trusted='*'          -> 307 https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/opcert/jobs

The `127.0.0.1` row reproduces the live `/review/` header byte for byte, and flipping only the trust
list flips only the scheme. That both confirms the mechanism and rejects the rival hypotheses
(nginx stripping the header; an app-side hardcoded scheme; an HSTS gap — HSTS is present and
server-level at `rebar.conf.template:98`). It also establishes that **opcert emits the identical
downgrade** to the one caller that can actually reach it: the guard-bearing API Gateway request,
i.e. the caller that carries a credential.

### Gerrit `location /` — CAN emit, but does NOT downgrade

Gerrit does emit absolute same-host Locations, and they are already `https`:

    /settings       -> 302  location: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/settings/
    /Documentation  -> 302  location: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/Documentation/index.html
    /login          -> 302  location: https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?...&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2F...

Because Gerrit builds them from `canonicalWebUrl = https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/`
(`infra/compose/gerrit.config:14`) rather than from a per-request forwarded scheme. So Gerrit is
**not** affected by root cause B — but its guarantee rests on one config value that nothing at the
edge enforces. It is the one surface where the ticket's original "missing structural guarantee,
not a reproduced downgrade" framing still holds exactly.

### Discovered, deliberately NOT fixed here

`/review/`'s Location also **loses the `/review/` prefix** (`…/review/health/` -> `…/health`, which
falls through to Gerrit and 404s). That is a separate path-correctness defect caused by the
prefix-stripping `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}/;` combined with an app that
builds absolute URLs from the public Host header. It is orthogonal to the scheme invariant this
ticket owns, it is not a security downgrade, and folding it in would widen the blast radius past
what this plan covers. Filed as a sibling with `discovered_from`.

### Fix shape (both layers, exactly as 79b2 did for MCP)

1. **Root cause.** Set `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS: "*"` on `review-bot` and `opcert`, so each app trusts
   nginx's forwarded proto and stops building `http://` URLs at the source. Bounded exactly as for
   `mcp`: both ports are published on host **loopback** with nginx the sole reachable client, and
   nginx sets `X-Forwarded-Proto https` as a **literal** that overwrites anything a client sends,
   so the value cannot be forged.
2. **Structural backstop.** Add per-location `proxy_redirect` http->https rules to `/review/`,
   `/opcert/` and Gerrit's `location /`, so no future upstream — or a Gerrit whose
   `canonicalWebUrl` drifts — can re-open the downgrade. **Per-location, never server-level**
   (79b2's binding precedent), and each block restates `proxy_redirect default;` first so the
   implicit default that nginx drops as soon as any explicit rule appears is preserved.

comments.body:
## Fix pushed for review — Gerrit change 2348

https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2348 (commit `a36c9b8031cf`, branch
`reb-a61d-proxy-redirect`). NOT submitted, NOT deployed; nginx on the box was not reloaded.

### The change (+229 lines, 3 files)

**`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`** — `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS: "*"` on `review-bot` and on
`opcert`, the root-cause layer. Exactly the value and the bounded-trust reasoning the `mcp`
service already carries: `"*"` rather than a pinned bridge-gateway address because neither
service declares a `networks:` block, so that address is implicit and can drift; trust-all is
bounded because both ports are published on host loopback with nginx the sole reachable client
and nginx sets `X-Forwarded-Proto https` as a literal that overwrites client input.

**`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template`** — the structural backstop on all three surfaces
(`/review/`, `/opcert/`, Gerrit `location /`), each block gaining:

    proxy_redirect default;
    proxy_redirect http://$host/          https://$host/;
    proxy_redirect http://127.0.0.1:PORT/ https://$host/;

**Per-location, never server-level** — 79b2's binding precedent, honoured. `proxy_redirect
default;` is restated FIRST in every block, because nginx drops a location's implicit default the
moment any explicit rule appears there; that restatement is what preserves `/review/`'s
prefix-stripping `default` rewrite (AC3), and the ordering matters because nginx evaluates rules
in sequence.

**`tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py`** — four new tests asserting on the RENDERED config
(reusing 2333's `_render_nginx()` helper) and on the committed compose file.

### AC status

- **AC1** — established for all three, recorded in the RCA comment above. `/review/` and
  `/opcert/` CAN emit (both reproduced); Gerrit CAN emit but does not downgrade
  (`canonicalWebUrl = https://…`).
- **AC2** — `test_nginx_upgrades_any_plaintext_location_on_the_sibling_surfaces`.
- **AC3** — `test_nginx_sibling_surfaces_restate_the_default_proxy_redirect`, which asserts
  `default` is present AND first.
- **AC4** — `test_nginx_gerrit_location_still_has_no_rewrite_and_no_proxy_pass_path`, which pins
  the reasoning (proxy_redirect touches only response headers) by failing if the backstop is ever
  turned into a `rewrite` or a URI path is added to Gerrit's `proxy_pass`.
- **AC5 (LIVE VALIDATION)** — **NOT met, and cannot be until this deploys.** It is the reason
  this ticket stays `in_progress`. The current live headers are recorded in the RCA comment above
  (the pre-fix state). Re-probe `/review/health/`, `/review/webhook/`, `/review/rerun/` and, with
  a valid `X-Opcert-Guard`, `/opcert/jobs/` after the deploy and record the actual headers here.

### Verification

**nginx syntax** — the rendered config was parsed by real nginx (`nginx -t` in a throwaway
`nginx:1.27-alpine` container, host-only externals stubbed): *syntax is ok / test is successful*.

**Mutation check — 16 mutants, all killed** (`--color=no`, judged on the pytest return code, not
on stdout text). Deleting each of the three rules from each of the three blocks (9), moving
`default` after the explicit rules in `/review/` and in Gerrit's block (2), adding a URI path to
Gerrit's `proxy_pass` (1), implementing the backstop as a `rewrite` (1), dropping
`FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` from each service (2), and pinning it to a bridge IP (1) each turn the
suite RED; restoring returns 52 passed.

**A first mutation round found a real oracle defect and it was fixed, not accepted.** Two mutants
initially SURVIVED — dropping `proxy_redirect default;` from Gerrit's block, and reordering it in
`/review/`. Cause: these blocks are heavily commented and the comments name the very directive
under test, so `re.findall(r"proxy_redirect\s+([^;]+);", body)` matched the *prose* and the oracle
passed on a config that no longer carried the rule. `_location_body()` now strips comment lines
before scanning, and both mutants die.

**Gates** — `make lint` clean; `make typecheck` clean (683 files); `pytest
tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` 4 passed; `check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
`active=39 new=0 increased=0 stale=10`. `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` 52 passed; the
wider related set (`test_mcp_on_box_infra` + `test_opcert_deploy_infra` + `test_review_bot` +
`test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen`) 210 passed.

### Deploy note (not actioned here)

`autodeploy.sh`'s blue-green `mcp_run_new()` spells out the `mcp` service's env as `-e` flags and
already carries `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS='*'` (`:380`). `review-bot` and `opcert` are started by
`docker compose`, which reads the compose file directly, so no autodeploy change is needed for
them — but they DO need a container restart for the new env to take effect, and nginx needs a
reload for the template change. Both happen on the next deploy.

## Close attempt — AC1-AC4 verified and ticked; AC5 (LIVE VALIDATION) FAILS: merged but NOT deployed

Merge SHA: **`25fd2cf6dd75`** ("Stop the sibling edge surfaces downgrading", Gerrit change 2348),
reachable from `origin/main` (`25ea12c200ae`). Verified in a fresh worktree detached at
`25ea12c200ae`: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 25fd2cf6dd75 HEAD` -> true.

**The ticket cannot be closed.** The code landed; the running system was never updated. Every
live probe below reproduces the ORIGINAL pre-fix downgrade, today.

---

### AC5 — LIVE VALIDATION: **NOT MET**

Unauthenticated probes of the deployed edge, no credential transmitted:

```
$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -D - https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/review/health/
HTTP/2 307
location: http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/health
strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains

$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -D - https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/review/webhook/
HTTP/2 307
location: http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/webhook

$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -D - https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/review/rerun/
HTTP/2 307
location: http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/rerun

$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -D - https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/opcert/jobs/
HTTP/2 403          (no Location — nginx X-Opcert-Guard rejects before proxying)

$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -D - https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/opcert/health/
HTTP/2 403          (no Location — same guard)

$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -D - https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/settings
HTTP/2 302
location: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/settings/

$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -D - https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/Documentation
HTTP/2 302
location: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/Documentation/index.html
```

**Liveness anchors — each probe is proven to have reached the surface under test, so no result
here is the vacuous "no Location because nothing happened".**

- `/review/` — anchored by an authentic review-bot application response, not a generic 404:
  ```
  $ curl -sS -D - https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/review/health
  HTTP/2 200
  server: nginx/1.30.2
  content-type: application/json
  {"status":"ok","in_flight":2,"queue_depth":3}
  ```
  That body is the review-bot's own health payload. The trailing-slash variant then ELICITS an
  actual redirect, so there IS a `Location` header to inspect — and it is `http://`. This
  distinguishes "correctly rewritten" from "no redirect happened": a redirect happened, and it
  downgraded.
- Gerrit `location /` — anchored by two real 302s carrying absolute same-host Locations
  (`/settings`, `/Documentation`), both already `https` from `canonicalWebUrl`.
- Control, to prove a generic miss looks different: `GET /zzz-nonexistent-surface/` -> `HTTP/2
  404`, no Location. None of the surfaces above returned that shape.
- `/opcert/` — the 403 is nginx's own fail-closed `X-Opcert-Guard` rejection, i.e. a recognisable
  response FROM the `/opcert/` location block rather than a fallthrough 404. **But it is
  explicitly NOT a pass**: nginx never proxies, so the `proxy_redirect` backstop under test never
  runs. Unauthenticated `/opcert/` cannot validate this criterion in either direction; it is
  untestable at this privilege posture, not satisfied by it.

### Why AC5 fails: the change merged but was never deployed

Read-only inspection of box `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` (`us-east-1`, via `aws ssm send-command`
running only `grep` / `ls` / `docker inspect` — no write, no reload, no restart):

```
$ grep -n proxy_redirect /etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf
165:        # level, NOT server level: proxy_redirect defaults to `default`, which is derived
168:        proxy_redirect http://$host/ https://$host/;
169:        proxy_redirect http://rebar_mcp/ https://$host/;
184:        proxy_redirect http://$host/ https://$host/;
185:        proxy_redirect http://rebar_mcp/ https://$host/;
203:        proxy_redirect http://$host/ https://$host/;
204:        proxy_redirect http://rebar_mcp/ https://$host/;

$ ls -la /etc/nginx/conf.d/
-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 12618 Aug 27 22:05 rebar.conf
```

The running config carries **only 79b2's three MCP `rebar_mcp` rules**. None of a61d's six new
sibling rules — the `/review/` `127.0.0.1:${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}` pair, the `/opcert/` `127.0.0.1:8090`
pair, the Gerrit `127.0.0.1:8080` pair, nor any of the three restated `proxy_redirect default;`
lines — is present. The file is dated **Aug 27 22:05**; a61d merged **Aug 28 15:16**.

The root-cause layer is equally absent:

```
$ docker inspect compose-review-bot-1 --format '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' | grep -i FORWARDED
(no match)
$ docker inspect compose-opcert-1 --format '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' | grep -i FORWARDED
(no match)
```

Neither container carries `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS`, so uvicorn still defaults to `"127.0.0.1"`,
still distrusts the docker-bridge peer, still drops `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, and Starlette
still builds `http://` absolute URLs — exactly the confirmed mechanism in the RCA comment.

Containers are `compose-review-bot-1 Up About an hour`, `compose-opcert-1 Up 24 hours`, i.e. the
restart the compose change needs has not happened either. Per the deploy note on the previous
comment, `review-bot` and `opcert` need a container restart and nginx needs a config
render + reload; neither occurred.

Note this is the `waspy-piecemeal-queenconch` failure mode's cousin: a pipeline reporting success
is not evidence of a redeploy. Here the running artefacts were read directly and they are stale.

---

### AC1 — MET (ticked)

Established and recorded for all three surfaces, in the Phase-1-exit RCA comment above, by
inspecting how each app builds redirects and its proxy-headers trust boundary:

- `/review/` **CAN** emit an absolute `http://` Location — reproduced live above.
- `/opcert/` **CAN** — same mechanism: `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` is set for the `mcp` service only
  (`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`), unset for `review-bot` and `opcert`; both are published on
  host loopback so nginx connects from the bridge gateway and is untrusted. Confirmed again today
  against the live containers (`docker inspect` output above).
- Gerrit `location /` **CAN** emit absolute same-host Locations but does **not** downgrade — it
  builds them from `canonicalWebUrl = https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/`
  (`infra/compose/gerrit.config:14`). Confirmed live: `/settings` and `/Documentation` both 302 to
  `https://`. Its guarantee rests on a config value nothing at the edge enforces, which is why it
  still gets the backstop.

### AC2 — MET (ticked)

`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template` at `25fd2cf6dd75` carries, per-location and never server-level:

```
/review/  :117 proxy_redirect default;
          :118 proxy_redirect http://$host/ https://$host/;
          :119 proxy_redirect http://127.0.0.1:${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}/ https://$host/;
/opcert/  :146 proxy_redirect default;
          :147 proxy_redirect http://$host/ https://$host/;
          :148 proxy_redirect http://127.0.0.1:8090/ https://$host/;
Gerrit /  :289 proxy_redirect default;
          :290 proxy_redirect http://$host/ https://$host/;
          :291 proxy_redirect http://127.0.0.1:8080/ https://$host/;
```

Structural test over the RENDERED template:
`tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py::test_nginx_upgrades_any_plaintext_location_on_the_sibling_surfaces`
plus `test_compose_sibling_services_trust_the_edge_forwarded_proto[review-bot]` and `[opcert]`.
Re-run today in a fresh worktree at `25ea12c200ae`: **7 passed, 45 deselected**.

### AC3 — MET (ticked)

`proxy_redirect default;` is restated FIRST in each of the three blocks (`:117`, `:146`, `:289`),
before any explicit rule, so nginx does not drop the implicit default and `/review/`'s
prefix-stripping rewrite survives. Pinned by
`test_nginx_sibling_surfaces_restate_the_default_proxy_redirect`, which asserts `default` is both
present AND first — passing.

### AC4 — MET (ticked)

`proxy_redirect` rewrites only the `Location`/`Refresh` **response** headers; it is not a
`rewrite` and adds no URI path to `proxy_pass`, so it cannot touch the request URI that Gerrit's
`%2F`-safe proxying depends on (standing constraint at `rebar.conf.template:245-252`). Pinned by
`test_nginx_gerrit_location_still_has_no_rewrite_and_no_proxy_pass_path`, which fails if the
backstop is ever turned into a `rewrite` or a path is added to Gerrit's `proxy_pass` — passing.
Corroborated live (current, pre-deploy edge): an encoded-slash Gerrit path proxies correctly —
`GET /projects/rebar/branches/refs%2Fheads%2Fmain` -> `HTTP/2 200`.

---

### Blocked — escalating rather than forcing

Ticket stays `in_progress`. The close gate is correct to refuse: AC5 is a genuine, currently
false assertion about the deployed system. Clearing it requires a **deploy** — rendering the
template and reloading nginx, and recreating `review-bot`/`opcert` with the new env — which is a
mutation of a shared box and needs operator approval before an agent performs it. No `--force`
was used and no gate was bypassed.

comments.body:
AC5's failure is explained, and the escalation to hand-deploy nginx is NOT needed — the pipeline is working, it is deferring.

Read-only inspection of i-00880b2c7f13527c5 (us-east-1): rebar-autodeploy.timer is ACTIVE and fires every ~2 minutes. Every tick since main advanced is emitting AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED with reason 'review-in-flight':

  ts 1787958006  in_flight=1  deferred_for=1142s  bound=2400s
  ts 1787958134  in_flight=1  deferred_for=1270s  bound=2400s
  ts 1787958264  in_flight=2  deferred_for=1400s  bound=2400s
  ts 1787958394  in_flight=2  deferred_for=1530s  bound=2400s
  ts 1787958524  in_flight=2  deferred_for=1660s  bound=2400s
  ts 1787958644  in_flight=1  deferred_for=1780s  bound=2400s

The pending target is 25ea12c200aea35eee057172c133eddcee2d0aa1, and 25fd2cf6dd75 (this ticket's fix) is confirmed an ANCESTOR of it — so the nginx rules and the FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS change both ride this deploy. The running /etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf dated Aug 27 22:05 is stale for exactly one reason: the drain gate has not let a deploy through since.

This is the class already recorded as bug 7b4a, and autodeploy.sh documents it in its own comments: in_flight is a CONCURRENT GAUGE while DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX is reasoned about as if it were a single-review timer, so an episode can be outlasted by ordinary PIPELINING rather than by any single long review. That is precisely the present state — a burst of parallel agent patchsets is holding the gauge at 1-2 continuously, so the episode never drains to 0.

Consequence for this ticket: AC5 is a true negative right now, and it is expected to clear WITHOUT any manual intervention once the deferral episode ends — either because in_flight reaches 0, or because deferred_for crosses the 2400s bound and the deploy proceeds anyway (emitting a countable bound-exceeded interrupt, at the cost of killing one in-flight review).

Recommended disposition: do NOT hand-render the template or reload nginx. That mutation carries a blast radius across every 443 surface including Gerrit and MCP, and would pre-empt a deploy that is already queued and imminent. Wait for the episode to clear, then RE-RUN the AC5 probes against the deployed edge and tick on that evidence. The cheapest way to shorten the episode is to stop pushing new patchsets for a few minutes, since each new patchset starts a review and re-arms the gauge.

That is exactly why the 23:21 deploy moved the MCP container to `rebar-mcp-25ea12c200ae-8092` while `/etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf` still shows `mtime=2026-08-27 22:05:26 +0000` with 7 `proxy_redirect` directives — the pre-a61d shape. Change `25fd2cf6dd75` is merged but not live and will stay that way indefinitely.

Filed as `downy-feminist-leopard` (1d1b-a719-b675-4a1f), linked relates_to here. This ticket is effectively blocked on that one: verifying a61d live at the edge requires the edge to actually deploy. compiled_state.description:
## Summary

Discovered by the Step 7 parity sweep while fixing `fernlike-toothsome-hen` (79b2-6ebc-6c1d-4125),
where the MCP edge emitted `307` with a plaintext `http://` Location on the documented client URL.

The **rule** that bug established: *an https request to this edge must never receive a `Location`
header that downgrades the scheme to `http`.* That rule is now enforced for the MCP paths only.
The other proxied surfaces on the same port-443 server have no equivalent guarantee.

## Channel census (`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template`)

| surface | Location-scheme guarantee |
|---|---|
| `location = /mcp/`, `= /mcp`, prefix `/mcp` | ENFORCED by 79b2 (`proxy_redirect` http->https) |
| `location /review/` (`:92`) | **MISSING** |
| `location /opcert/` (`:107`) | **MISSING** |
| `location /` -> Gerrit (`:152`) | **MISSING** |
| port-80 server | N/A — correctly `301`s to https |

HSTS is NOT part of this gap: 79b2 adds `add_header Strict-Transport-Security ... always;` at the
443 **server** level, so every surface above already inherits that backstop.

## Why it was left out of 79b2's scope

The obvious fix — hoisting `proxy_redirect` to the server level — is NOT safe as a drop-in.
`proxy_redirect` defaults to `default`, which derives its rewrite from **that location's own**
`proxy_pass`. `/review/` uses `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}/;` (a
prefix-stripping form), so its `default` rule rewrites the upstream's `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/`
Location back to `/review/`. Declaring explicit server-level rules would REPLACE that default and
could break the review-bot's relative redirects. Gerrit's block additionally carries a standing
"do not add a rewrite here" constraint for `%2F`-safe proxying (`:145-151`) — `proxy_redirect`
only touches response headers, never the request URI, so it is very likely safe there, but that
needs to be established rather than assumed.

So the correct fix is per-surface and needs its own verification, which is more than 79b2's
blast radius should carry.

## Severity

Lower than 79b2. No plaintext Location has been OBSERVED from these three surfaces; this is a
missing structural guarantee, not a reproduced downgrade. The 79b2 root cause B
(`FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` unset, so uvicorn distrusts the forwarded proto) applies specifically to
the containerised MCP service; `/review/` and `/opcert/` should be checked for the same posture
rather than presumed affected or unaffected.

## Root cause (CONFIRMED — supersedes the "not reproduced" severity note above)

The downgrade IS reproduced, on `/review/`, unauthenticated, against the deployed edge:

    GET https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/review/health/
      -> HTTP/2 307, location: http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/health

(`/review/webhook/` and `/review/rerun/` behave identically.) Full evidence in the Phase-1-exit
RCA comment.

Mechanism — this is 79b2's **root cause B on two more services**, answering this ticket's own open
question: `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` is set only for the `mcp` service (`docker-compose.yml:357`,
`autodeploy.sh:380`) and is **unset** for `review-bot` (`:75`) and `opcert` (`:266`). uvicorn
defaults it to `"127.0.0.1"` and wraps each app in `ProxyHeadersMiddleware(trusted_hosts=<that>)`.
Both run in containers published on host loopback (`:97`, `:298`), so nginx connects from the
docker bridge gateway, the peer is untrusted, `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` is dropped,
`scope["scheme"]` stays `"http"`, and Starlette's `redirect_slashes` builds an absolute
`URL(scope=…)` at `http://`. Flipping only the trust list flips only the scheme, for both apps.

Gerrit is NOT affected by that mechanism: it builds absolute Locations from
`canonicalWebUrl = https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/` (`infra/compose/gerrit.config:14`) and
already emits https (`/settings` -> `https://…/settings/`). Its guarantee is a config value that
nothing at the edge enforces, so it still warrants the backstop.

## Approach

Two layers, mirroring exactly what 79b2 did for MCP:

1. **Root cause** — `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`: set `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS: "*"` on
   `review-bot` and `opcert`, so each app trusts nginx's forwarded proto and stops building
   `http://` URLs at the source. `"*"` rather than a pinned bridge-gateway address for the same
   reason the `mcp` service documents: neither service declares a `networks:` block, so that
   address is implicit and can drift, and a stale pin re-opens the downgrade with no failure
   signal. Trust-all is bounded here — both ports are published on host **loopback** with nginx
   the sole reachable client, and nginx sets `X-Forwarded-Proto https` as a **literal** that
   overwrites anything a client sends, so the value cannot be forged.
2. **Structural backstop** — `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template`: add `proxy_redirect` http->https
   rules to `/review/` (`:103`), `/opcert/` (`:118`) and Gerrit's `location /` (`:253`).
   **Per-location, never server-level** — 79b2's binding precedent, because a server-level rule
   would REPLACE each location's `default`. Each block therefore restates `proxy_redirect
   default;` FIRST, since nginx drops the implicit default as soon as any explicit rule appears in
   a location; that is what preserves `/review/`'s prefix-stripping default rewrite.

`proxy_redirect` rewrites only the `Location`/`Refresh` **response** headers. It is not a
`rewrite` and adds no URI path to `proxy_pass`, so it cannot affect Gerrit's `%2F`-safe request
proxying, which is governed by the standing constraint at `rebar.conf.template:245-252`.

Deliberately out of scope: `/review/`'s Location also loses the `/review/` prefix
(`…/review/health/` -> `…/health`). That is path correctness, not a scheme downgrade, and is filed
as a sibling via `discovered_from`.

## Testing

- Happy path: the RENDERED config (template through `envsubst '${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}'`) shows each of
  the three locations carrying both the `$host` and the upstream-form http->https `proxy_redirect`
  rules.
- Edge: each of the three restates `proxy_redirect default;` before its explicit rules, so no
  implicit default is dropped — the direct evidence for `/review/`'s prefix-stripping rewrite
  surviving.
- Compose posture: `review-bot` and `opcert` each set `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` to exactly `"*"`,
  asserted against the committed `docker-compose.yml` the way the existing `mcp` test does.
- Mutation check: deleting each new rule / env value in turn must turn the corresponding test RED.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] For each of `/review/`, `/opcert/` and Gerrit's `location /`, it is established and
      recorded whether that upstream can emit an absolute `http://` Location — by inspecting how
      each app builds redirects and whether it sits behind a proxy-headers trust boundary.
- [x] Every surface that CAN emit one carries a `proxy_redirect` rule upgrading it to `https`,
      added per-location so no existing `default` rule is replaced. Verified by a structural test
      over `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template` that fails if a surface regresses.
- [x] `/review/`'s existing `default` proxy_redirect behaviour is preserved — evidenced by
      showing the prefix-stripping rewrite still applies after the change.
- [x] Gerrit's `%2F`-safe proxying is unaffected, evidenced by reasoning or a probe that
      `proxy_redirect` alters only response headers and not the request URI.
- [ ] LIVE VALIDATION [non-codebase]: an unauthenticated probe of each surface on the deployed
      edge shows no `http://` Location, recorded in a comment with the actual response headers.
        provenance: environment=deployed edge https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com (EC2 i-00880b2c7f13527c5, us-east-1); principal=anonymous public client (no credential transmitted) plus read-only SSM inspection of the box as the operator's AWS identity; privilege_posture=unauthenticated for every HTTP probe, read-only for every on-box command (no write, no reload, no restart); instrument=curl -sS -D - over HTTPS, and aws ssm send-command AWS-RunShellScript running only grep/ls/docker inspect — the scheme of a Location header emitted by the live edge is observable only from the deployed box and cannot be established from repository state, and this criterion is currently NOT met: the merged fix is present in the repository but absent from the running configuration.

## Notes

Reported from unauthenticated probes and repo inspection only. No credential was transmitted.
